title: How does the brain store memories?
subtitle: Memory & neurons
subject: sciences
description: Memory is not a library of drawers. It is a living network of neurons that reinforce each other, rebuild themselves and sometimes make mistakes.

hero.hook: A memory is not a file: it is a path that the brain has learned to redo.

blocks.text: We often imagine memory as a hard drive. In reality, it is a living network. Billions of **neurons**, nerve cells, reconnect, strengthen or weaken depending on what we experience.
Nothing is stored in one place. A memory is a distributed trace, fragile at the beginning, more solid after sleep, and always a little reconstructed when we remember it.

Between two neurons, the point of contact is called a **synapse**, the junction where the nerve signal passes. The human brain has approximately **86 billion** neurons and more than **100,000 billion** synapses.

blocks.caption: The hippocampus plays a central role in the formation of memories.

blocks.text: When information is repeated or linked to a strong emotion, the same neurons activate together. Their link becomes easier to trigger: it is , the lasting strengthening of synapses. The more a circuit is used, the “wider” the path becomes. A memory is therefore not a stored object, but a **trace** in the network. [[Long-term potentiation (LTP)]]
The brain's storage capacity is estimated at approximately **2.5 petabytes**, the equivalent of millions of hours of video. But it is not a disc: it is a living tissue that is reorganizing itself.

The **seahorse**, a small structure in the , region behind the temples, does not keep memories forever. It receives them, **encode**, transforms them into memory traces, then redistributes them to the **cortex**, the outer layer of the brain. This transfer is called **consolidation**. [[temporal lobe]]

It is mainly done during **sleep**. Without a functioning hippocampus, we can live in the present moment, but we no longer hold new conscious memories. We remain stuck in a present without a recent past.

Patient **H.M.**, operated on in 1953, no longer formed new memories. However, he progressed every day at drawing in a mirror, without remembering having already tried: his memory of the gestures was intact.

Recalling a memory is not replaying a video. Each time you take it out, it becomes **malleable**, modifiable. Our current emotions, our new knowledge or a suggestion can modify it before it is “re-recorded”.

Psychologist **Elizabeth Loftus** showed that you can implant **false memories** with simple questions. Hence the caution today in the face of eyewitness testimony: in good faith, the brain fills in the gaps.

sections.title: Multiple memories in a single brain

blocks.text: The memory of facts and life episodes, what we can tell, passes mainly through the hippocampus. The , that of cycling or swimming, depends instead on the **cerebellum**, a structure at the back of the brain, and other older structures. [[Procedural memory]]
This is why some amnesia patients forget their own name but still play the piano. Memory is not a single drawer: it is a mosaic of systems.
A memory is a dynamic trace: synapses reinforced, consolidated especially at night, and rebuilt with each reminder. It is never a fixed file.
